wbcp_threshold.title: How WBCP turns a calibration bank into a threshold
wbcp_threshold.caption: WBCP on a real TD3+BC hopper bank. Each Bayesian-bootstrap draw of the score CDF (masses on the scores plus a never-covered test atom) crosses 1 - alpha once. BCA deploys the 95%-credible crossing, not the empirical 90% point, and the margin shrinks as the bank grows. 'misses' is each threshold's true miscoverage on the rest of the pool.
wbcp_threshold.takeaway: The empirical quantile alone sits on the truth and can miss more than alpha. WBCP deploys the beta-credible crossing of its posterior, which adds a margin that is large for small banks and shrinks with n.

shift_weighting.title: Importance weights under shift: uniform BQ-CP vs WBCP
shift_weighting.caption: On a real hopper pool tilted toward sparse states, the uniform threshold (orange) is exact for the calibration law but misses 13% of test rows. WBCP's importance weights push the threshold right and cut bank failures from 89.5% to 7.55% at gamma = 1, at the cost of a smaller effective sample (n_eff 391 of 1,103).
shift_weighting.takeaway: Under covariate shift, uniform BQ-CP certifies the wrong law and fails up to 100% of banks. WBCP's weights bring failures back near the 5% budget (7.55% at gamma = 1, a finite-sample excess) by trading effective sample size for a wider, more conservative threshold.

bank_dependence.title: Why the calibration bank is thinned
bank_dependence.caption: Rows within an episode are correlated, so a bank of whole episodes behaves like far fewer independent rows (design effect D) and fails 27–48% of the time. BCA's thinned bank (a few spaced rows from each of many withheld episodes) brings D near 1, and failures near the 5% budget.
bank_dependence.takeaway: Whole-episode banks fail 27–48% because within-episode correlation inflates the design effect. Thinning to a few spaced rows per episode restores about 5% (hopper: 5.1%), with K set by each dataset's measured rho.

critic_alignment.title: Calibrating the critic the actor actually follows
critic_alignment.caption: a, Illustration, exact LQ-harness Q: when Q1 is optimistic and Q2 accurate, min(Q1, Q2) equals Q2, so the residual BCA calibrated carries none of Q1's error. b, real frozen D4RL TD3+BC critics: the min-calibrated band fails for Q1's residual in 10-82% of 4,000 banks. Calibrating Q1 brings this to 4.0-5.1%, at 2-10% more width.
critic_alignment.takeaway: A band calibrated on min(Q1, Q2) does not certify the Q1 that TD3+BC's actor climbs: 10-82% of banks fail against a 5% budget. Calibrating Q1 restores validity at 2-10% more width.

bc_dose.title: Width to BC dose: same mean, unequal strength
bc_dose.caption: BCA maps the certified width to a BC multiplier bounded below 1.5. On five real D4RL pools, the per-row doses sit near 1.3 and spread little, so in practice the dose acts as nearly uniform extra BC (a). Post hoc, in the step-3 LQ harness: a dose with the same mean is not a dose of the same strength. The oracle's BC gradient was 2-3× the constant dose's in the one case where it moved J a lot (b).
bc_dose.takeaway: BCA's dose acts as about 1.3× nearly uniform extra BC, and step 3's oracle "targeting" effect was mostly strength, so the controls must match realized strength, not mean dose.

pipeline.title: BCA pipeline: from training to testing
pipeline.caption: How BCA works in each host. The host trains on the episodes that are not withheld. At each refresh, BCA scores a thinned held-out bank with the current critic and sets a WBCP (uniform = BQ-CP) threshold. Between refreshes, the frozen width becomes a detached dose on one host loss term. Four tests check the pieces; their status is marked.
pipeline.takeaway: BCA calibrates a held-out one-step residual and turns it into a detached multiplier on one host loss term. Threshold validity and the known-MDP signal test are done. Placement is still running and full D4RL training is next.
